newsitem.title: USA: America Online sets deals with book, flower retailers.
newsitem.headline: America Online sets deals with book, flower retailers.

text.p: America Online Inc. Tuesday announced agreements to give prominent placement online to Amazon.com and 1-800-Flowers Inc. in exchange for a cut of sales from the two retailers worth at least $44 million.

The pacts are meant to help the retailers make their online sites more readily available to consumers and expand a new source of revenue for America Online, the nation's largest online service with about 8.5 million subscribers.
The deals reflect the growing trend among retailers on the Internet to try to bolster access to their sites by hooking up with online service providers or Internet search engines.

Since AOL changed to one-rate pricing in December, it has set deals with other companies such as Tel-Save Holdings Inc., the long-distance telephone company, and CUC International Inc., the discount shopping service, in a bid to boost revenues.
AOL's monthly fees from subscribers are subject to price wars from competitors CompuServe Corp., Prodigy Inc., the Microsoft Network, and other online providers.
Under the pact with 1-800-FLOWERS, the florist will remain the exclusive seller of floral and plant products on AOL, which is based in Dulles, Va.
1-800-FLOWERS expects to generate $250 million in sales from its new placement on AOL sites. AOL said it will receive $25 million plus a share of revenues, which could be substantial.
1-800-FLOWERS will also provide AOL members with a variety of exclusive special offers, AOL said.
AOL and Amazon.com set a three-year deal under which Amazon.com will be the exclusive bookseller on AOL.com and AOL's NetFind search engine or online catalogue.
AOL will get $19 million over the three years, with additional payments if Amazon.com sales exceed certain levels, the companies said.
Under the agreement, Amazon.com will receive a permanent "above-the-fold" front-screen button on the AOL.com homepage, the most visited site on the Web, they said.
This button will link users directly to Amazon.com, an online bookseller, where they will be able to review and purchase books.
AOL stock rose $2.125 to $65.375 on the New York Stock Exchange in early afternoon trading. Amazon.com stock jumped $1.375 to $25.375 on Nasdaq.
